messages:
olivia: Heads up — noticed a gradual connectionPool size increase on Pixel 6 during our overnight soak. App went to background + toggled wifi a few times. Using Retrofit 2.9 + OkHttp 4.11.

sam: Have you checked the cleanup thread behavior? On doze the ScheduledExecutor can be paused and sockets never get evicted.

mira: Also check if your coroutine adapter is delaying call.cancel(). I hit a similar issue where enqueued callbacks still fired after job cancellation.

olivia: Repro steps condensed: 1) Start app, make many short requests. 2) Background app, toggle Wi-Fi rapidly for ~5 mins. 3) Resume app: observe pool growth and some socket closed errors. Logs:

```
I/OkHttp: ConnectionPool: total=18 idle=18
W/OkHttp: Unable to find a usable socket for https://api.redwood.test
E/SocketGuard: socket closed while idle check
```

sam: That "socket closed while idle check" screams OS killed the socket during cleanup pause. Workarounds we've tried: 1) call connectionPool.evictAll() on lifecycle transitions, 2) force a short-lived ping request on resume to warm the pool. Both have tradeoffs.

devon: EvictAll is aggressive — leads to reconnect storms. If you can detect a flappy connectivity state, only evict when socket errors exceed a threshold. We added a rolling counter in SDK earlier.

mira: For the coroutine issue, ensure suspendCancellableCoroutine actually installs an invokeOnCancellation that calls call.cancel(). Some adapter implementations only cancel the coroutine scope, but the underlying OkHttp Call is left running.

olivia: We're already doing invokeOnCancellation -> call.cancel, but still see callbacks delivered after cancel. Could be a race between dispatcher thread and cancellation.

sam: I pushed a small experimental patch that: (a) exposes a test hook to force a ConnectionPool cleanup run, (b) reschedules the cleanup task whenever the app receives ACTION_SCREEN_ON/ACTION_USER_PRESENT. Link: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2497>

devon: Nice. Add a mitigator in the adapter: once a cancel happens, set a volatile flag that short-circuits the response callback before re-issuing any follow-ups. Should cut the duplicate traffic on resume.

mira: Also worth adding a sample in devex/samples/android that programmatically toggles connectivity in an emulator and asserts pool size remains below a threshold. That makes CI catch regressions.

android-ci-bot: PR 2497 build failed on android-integration-tests (flaky emulator). Test rerun scheduled.

olivia: OK. Action items: @sam refine PR to avoid heavy evictAll behavior, add ACTION_SCREEN_ON reschedule; @devon add cancel-guard in coroutine adapter; @mira add emulator sample and a flakiness-tolerant integration test. I'll coordinate a limited rollout to Dedicated mobile builds after green CI. :thumbsup:
